root_cause.text: The class, subclass, and protocol fields of the RNDIS function configuration options (f_rndis_opts) are read in rndis_bind without holding the existing mutex, creating a race condition with concurrent configfs writes.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states these options are "suspectible to race conditions as they can be accessed concurrently through configfs." The patch adds `scoped_guard(mutex, &rndis_opts->lock)` around the reads of `rndis_opts->class`, `rndis_opts->subclass`, and `rndis_opts->protocol` in `rndis_bind`, confirming the missing synchronization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add include for linux/cleanup.h to allow use of resource cleanup macros.
intent_record.what: Added #include <linux/cleanup.h> to the include list, placing it after the comment block and before the existing includes.
intent_record.how: This makes the kernel's cleanup macros (e.g., __free, scoped_guard) available in the compilation unit, enabling automatic resource management and scope-based guard patterns.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect access to RNDIS function configuration options with a mutex to prevent data races.
intent_record.what: Wrapped three assignments to rndis_iad_descriptor fields (bFunctionClass, bFunctionSubClass, bFunctionProtocol) inside a scoped_guard that acquires the mutex lock on rndis_opts->lock.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that reading rndis_opts->class, subclass, and protocol is serialized with the mutex, preventing race conditions when these fields are modified concurrently from other threads.
